evidence_note: Encodes the month-of-birth section of Iqqur ipus (section 64) from an open Oracc-served edition, together with the non-inference, calendar-gate and refusal rules that keep it from becoming a customer claim. This is the corpus's first non-horoscope Babylonian natal material; it is a menology, not a horoscopy, and the pack says so.

conclusion.reasoning: this witness is an abridged tabular recension that records, for each section, the months in which the act is favourable; it does not record unfavourable verdicts, so a month's absence is silence and not a negative judgment

exceptions: Do not complement the favourable list into an unfavourable list.

conclusion.statement: section 64 judges the birth by the month in which it happens; no planet, no zodiacal sign, no day and no hour enter it
conclusion.relation_to_the_horoscopes: this is a menology, structurally distinct from the Babylonian horoscope corpus already encoded in this repository, which does record celestial positions at birth

conclusion.form: abridged tabular Iqqur ipus on the obverse; list of lucky days and commented protases on the reverse
conclusion.self_description: the colophon presents the tablet as a list of “Favorable days, which are good to accomplish any plan, and for a person to achieve any goal”, compiled from tablets that came from Babylon, together with twenty-five lines extracted from a mukallimtu-commentary
conclusion.controlling_edition_not_open: the serie mensuelle, in which each month's prognoses are gathered under the month, is edited by Labat 1965 and was not retrievable in open form during this pass
conclusion.consequence: no claim is made here about the full wording of section 64 in the serie mensuelle

conclusion.grounds: the verdict is a favourability judgment on the act of being born in a month, recovered from a single abridged witness, without the controlling edition, and with no attested apodosis about the person; the corpus records it and does not say it
conclusion.what_the_section_may_say: that a month-of-birth layer exists in Babylonian menology, which months this witness marks favourable, and that the product declines to apply it
